The ﬁrst challenge is how to effectively represent a table, which is semi-structured and includes many aspects such as headers, cells and caption. The second chal- lenge is how to build a robust model that mea- sures the relevance between an unstructured nat- ural language query and a semi-structured table. Table retrieval could be viewed as a multi-modal task because the query and the table are of differ- ent forms.

[6] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 2 | Section: None
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
A table t is a set of data elements arranged by vertical columns and horizontal rows. Formally, we deﬁne a table as a triple t = {headers, cells, caption} that con- sists of three aspects. A table could have multiple headers, each of which indicates the property of a column and could be used to identify a column. A table could have multiple cells, each of which is a unit where a row and a column intersects. A table could have a caption, which is typically an explanatory text about the table.

[7] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
In this work, we focus on content-based table retrieval. Given a query, the task is to ﬁnd the most relevant table from a collection of tables. Further progress towards improving this area requires powerful models of semantic matching and richer training and evalua- tion resources. To remedy this, we present a ranking based approach, and implement both carefully designed features and neu- ral network architectures to measure the relevance between a query and the con- tent of a table.

[8] Source: 1706.02427.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: None
Title: Content-Based Table Retrieval for Web Queries
A table has different types of information, in- cluding headers, cells and caption. We develop different mechanisms to match the relevance be- tween a query and each aspect of a table. An important property of a table is that randomly exchanging two rows or tow columns will not change the meaning of a table (Vinyals et al., 2015). Therefore, a matching model should en- sure that exchanging rows or columns will result in the same output.

We can ﬁnd that in general the performance of an aspect in designed features is consistent with its performance in neu- ral networks. Caption is the most effective aspect on WebQueryTable. This is reasonable as we ﬁnd that majority of the queries are asking about a list of objects, such as “polish rivers”, “world top 5 mountains” and “list of american cruise lines”.

answer: Yes. The method has a dedicated mechanism for matching headers: it develops different mechanisms to match a query against each aspect of a table, including headers, cells, and caption [8]; it represents each header as an embedding vector and treats the set of header embeddings as external memory, assigning a probability to each header embedding given the query vector [13]; and it then obtains a query-specific header vector through weighted average [14]. Thus the method relies on the column headings of the table.
